title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are notes accompanying the May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals and Barsotti–Tate (BT) groups. The section heading on the previous page reads 'Prolongements infinitésimaux d'extensions de groupes de B.T.: conséquences pour la structure infinitésimale des schémas modulaires'.

(1) Upper part. We are given an extension E of a BT group M by a BT group N over a base S, which lies over a base R. S^(∞) denotes a formal infinitesimal neighbourhood, probably of S, or of the diagonal of S in S×_R S. G (written = S̃) is presumably a formal moduli object. The local pieces glue ('se recollent') to a morphism of formal (pre)schemes S^(∞) → G. Knowing this morphism is equivalent to knowing the extension E. The equivalence holds not over S itself but over the infinitesimal neighbourhood of S relative to R, together with the descent/compatibility isomorphism after base change. In modern terms this is the classifying map to a formal moduli space: the extension, viewed on the infinitesimal neighbourhood, is the pull-back of a universal one. This is the crystalline philosophy that the 'infinitesimal structure' of a family is read off from the moduli. The formation of S^(∞) → G commutes with base change S' → S. Grothendieck therefore says it should be understood as coming from a 'modular' situation, i.e. from a universal formal deformation space.

(2) Lower part. The modular situation is made precise:
- R = Spec A, with A a complete local (noetherian) ring with residue field k of characteristic p. A Cohen ring or Λ = W(k) is the typical example.
- M_0 and N_0 are BT groups over k, with N_0 of multiplicative type.
- ξ_0 is an extension of M_0 by N_0.
- The object sought is the formal moduli variety over R (a formal scheme) of deformations of ξ_0.
- One also considers the moduli space for the trivial extension.

The next page gives the results:
(i) The deformation space of the trivial extension is a smooth formal group, by functoriality (Baer sum). It is a formal torus T_p(M_0)^∨ ⊗ N_0. This is the Serre–Tate description of the local moduli of an ordinary BT group / ordinary abelian variety, with the étale part M_0 and multiplicative part N_0.
(ii) The moduli space for a nontrivial ξ_0 is a torsor under that torus.
(iii) For N_0 only radicial (connected), the deformation space of E_0 maps to the deformation space of N_0. Over that space it is a torsor under N_Y ⊗ T_p(E_0)^∨.

The page itself contains only the setup: the universal classifying morphism and its base-change compatibility, motivating formal moduli of extensions.

Correctness: the statements are consistent with known theory (Serre–Tate 1964; Messing 1972; Katz 1981). In the radicial case the torsor group should involve the étale quotient's Tate module, Hom(T_p(M_0), N) ≅ N ⊗ T_p(M_0)^∨; the next page's 'T_p(E_0)^∨' is equivalent when M_0 is étale.
errors: No mathematical error visible on this page; it is a set-up. On the next page, 'T_p(E_0)^∨' should be read as the Tate module of the étale quotient (M_0 étale); for general M_0 the stated torsor structure needs M_0 étale or must be interpreted as Hom(M_0, N)-type deformation data.
The phrase 'Supposons N_0 de t.m.' is left only implicitly paired with M_0 étale. The formal-torus statement (Serre–Tate) requires M_0 étale (ordinary case), which the page does not state explicitly.

ideas.what: An extension of BT groups over the infinitesimal neighbourhood is equivalent to a classifying morphism S^(∞) → G of formal schemes, compatible with base change, hence coming from a formal moduli space
ideas.modern_name: Classifying map to the universal formal deformation space (pro-representability of deformations of BT groups / extensions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1970 ICM 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'), Illusie (1985 'Déformations de groupes de Barsotti-Tate'), Messing (1972)
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (Actes ICM Nice 1970); Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1974)

ideas.what: Formal moduli of deformations of an extension of an étale BT group by a multiplicative one is a formal torus T_p(M_0)^∨ ⊗ N_0; nontrivial extensions give torsors
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate canonical coordinates / Serre–Tate local moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre and Tate (Woods Hole 1964), written up by Messing (1972) and Katz (1981)
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in the 1970 ICM talk; standard reference is Katz, 'Serre–Tate local moduli' (1981)

ideas.what: For N_0 radicial, the deformation space of E_0 is a torsor over the deformation space of N_0 under N ⊗ T_p^∨ (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Deformations of BT groups with étale quotient as torsors over the deformations of the connected part (connected–étale sequence deformation theory)

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up formal moduli of extensions of BT groups and their classifying maps. This is the Serre–Tate/Messing/Katz circle of ideas, well documented and partly announced by Grothendieck himself in 1970. The only point of mild interest is seeing him derive the Serre–Tate torus and its torsor generalization as a by-product of crystalline infinitesimal extension theory around 1966. Even that is anticipated by known history.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2: 'les liens se recollent et définissent un lien des positions formelles' should probably read 'ces termes/morphismes se recollent et définissent un morphisme de préschémas formels'.
'dont la connaissance [-implique-] {+équivaut à+}': the insertion appears to read 'équivaut à' or 'équivalente à'; the deleted word is uncertain.
'non par sur S lui-même' should read 'non pas sur S lui-même'.
'Il se recommande donc' is probably 'Il se reconnaît donc' or similar.
'Supposons N_0 de 1-...' should read 'Supposons N_0 de t.m.' (type multiplicatif), consistent with the next page.
'de car.[?] résiduelle p' is correct: 'de car. résiduelle p'.
The symbol before 'de M_0 par N_0' near the bottom is ξ_0 (an extension), written over a crossed-out symbol.
